title: Input, Events and User Interface
introduction: Unity input becomes gameplay intent, while events keep interface updates separate from the systems that own state.
learningOutcomes: Separate device input from gameplay intent.
Use events to notify independent components.
Update UI from authoritative game state.

activities.question: Why map an input action named Jump instead of checking one keyboard key everywhere?
options: The gameplay intent can support different devices and bindings
It removes the need for testing
activities.explanation: An action represents intent independently of a particular control.

activities.question: A health bar should become the authoritative owner of player health.
activities.explanation: The gameplay model owns health; the UI presents that state.

activities.question: A notification that interested listeners can subscribe to is an ___.
activities.explanation: Events reduce direct dependencies between the sender and its listeners.
